final_answer:
Depth-first search (DFS) and breadth-first search (BFS) are both algorithms used to traverse or search graphs. DFS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, while BFS explores all the neighbors at the current depth level before moving to the next level. 

DFS uses a stack (or recursion) and is useful for finding paths in mazes, topological sorting, and cycle detection. BFS uses a queue and is ideal for finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs or analyzing social networks. 

Choose DFS when the solution is likely deep in the graph or when memory efficiency is a concern. Opt for BFS when the shortest path is required or when exploring all nodes at a certain depth is necessary.
